text:
pagerbot: PagerDuty: HIGH - suspicious outbound S3 activity from inference-prod-03 detected. Possible debug log upload containing auth headers. Pager: @sam oncall.

sam: on it. tell me quick tl;dr — where is traffic going?

pagerbot: 3xx PUTs to s3://redwood-debug-uploads/ from instance inference-prod-03 (10.4.12.7). Pattern: debug-ish filenames, some contain 'auth' string.

ben: I can see the same in logs. quick grep showed lines like: `PUT /redwood-debug-uploads/logs/prod/2026-03-18/inference-prod-03-debug.log` with `Authorization:` snippets.

maria: ack. tagging sec-eng. we need containment then rotation. assume secrets exposure until proven otherwise.

lee: can we cordon the instance and suspend any debug log agents? I can run a script to stop the forwarder.

sam: yes cordon > stop forwarder. lee, drop steps here.

lee: `kubectl cordon inference-prod-03` then `kubectl scale deployment debug-log-forwarder --replicas=0 -n infra`. that stops new uploads.

erica: customer-facing triage — do we have any customers impacted? any PII in those logs?

ben: initial peek: two files uploaded in the last 30m. filenames: `prod-inference-03-debug-2026-03-18.log` and `prod-inference-03-kvcache-dump-2026-03-18.log`. kvcache dump looks trove-y.

maria: lee, after cordon and scale, snapshot the pod and copy its env for forensics. don't delete anything yet.

lee: copying env and tarballing /var/log/forwarder. running: `kubectl exec -n infra forwarder-pod -- tar czf /tmp/forwarder-env.tar.gz /etc/forwarder/* /var/log/forwarder`

sam: jordan-legal, FYI — potential log leakage with auth header fragments. need guidance on customer notice and retention.

jordan-legal: acknowledged. preserve chain-of-custody. legal needs a list of affected orgs and a data inventory for those files. hold notifications until we confirm scope (but keep stakeholders updated).

maria: rotate any creds that could be in the logs. priority: service-account keys used by inference-prod-03, S3 write creds scoped to debug bucket, and any short-lived tokens discovered. I'll coordinate.

ben: quick question: are these service-account keys or app-level keys? my traces show the forwarder used an STS-assumed role from infra-deploy-profile.

maria: rotate the role's access keys/credentials + revoke active STS sessions referencing that role. also add block rule to S3 bucket to deny public/unauthenticated list/put while we investigate.

lee: applying temporary S3 bucket policy deny for PUTs from non-admins. pushing change now.

sam: can we get a list of files and hash them for later review? also confirm whether those two files were accessed externally after upload.

ben: listing now: `aws s3api list-objects --bucket redwood-debug-uploads --prefix logs/prod/2026-03-18/` returns 2 keys with sizes 9.1MB and 48.3MB. will run `head` on them and save checksums.

ben: checksum results: a1b2c3d4... and f6e5d4c3... (saved to internal forensic bucket `forensics-temp`). access logs show PUTs from IP 203.0.113.45 (our egress NAT) only — no GETs observed.

maria: good — no external GETs so far. still treat as compromised. start key rotation plan: 1) create new credentials for infra-deploy-role 2) update deployment to use new creds (or rotate provider) 3) revoke old keys 4) audit for usage. I'll run the key rotation.

lee: i'm isolating the forwarder host: `kubectl drain inference-prod-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then will snapshot.

erica: support, please prepare a brief internal summary for potential customer comms: timeline, affected bucket, mitigation steps, and whether any customer-level identifiers were observed. keep language high-level.

erica: drafting now. who owns the final sign-off? jordan-legal for notifications and sec-eng for technical accuracy.

jordan-legal: yes that's correct.

sam: any indication of cause? deploy bug, misconfigured debug agent, or malicious actor?

ben: preliminary hypothesis: debug-forwarder was left enabled in prod rollout (bad config) and collected verbose logs that included partial auth headers. upload triggered by cron job during a debug ramp. no sign yet of lateral movement.

maria: treat as probable misconfig + exposure. prioritize rotation and forensics. I'll run `revoke-session` for STS tokens referencing infra-deploy-role and rotate IAM keys immediately.

lee: rotation in progress. I'm patching k8s secret `infra-deploy-creds` with new creds and restarting debug-forwarder (once we re-enable it safely).

ben: all steps logged in incident ticket INC-1999. saving artifacts to `forensics-temp` and locking access.

erica: timeline summary draft:
- 19:02 UTC: Pagerbot alerted on suspicious S3 PUTs from inference-prod-03
- 19:03: Sam acknowledged and oncall mobilized
- 19:05: Cordoned node, scaled down forwarder to stop uploads
- 19:09: Two candidate files identified and snapshotted to forensics-temp
- 19:12: No GETs observed; external access unlikely
- 19:14: Key rotation and STS revocation initiated

erica: i'll attach that to the ticket. please add any edits.

maria: once rotation completes, run a quick regression on inference traffic to ensure no auth failures for customers. plan a controlled rollout of new creds.

sam: thanks team. will keep this thread as the operational stream. any blockers escalate here. :thumbsup:
